title: NPS Remittance Delays: Finance Ministry Mandates Interest for Late Credits
description: The Finance Ministry has issued a stern warning regarding delays in depositing National Pension System (NPS) contributions. Employers must pay interest to sub.

faq.q: What is the deadline for NPS contributions for salaried employees?
faq.a: Generally, employers are expected to remit the NPS contributions deducted from employees' salaries within a few days of the salary disbursement, typically by the 10th or 15th of the subsequent month.

faq.q: How do I know if my NPS contribution is delayed?
faq.a: You can check your NPS transaction statement by logging into the Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA) system (NSDL or KFintech) using your PRAN. Compare the credit dates with your salary deduction dates.

faq.q: What is the PPF interest rate currently used for compensation?
faq.a: The compensatory interest for delayed NPS remittances will be calculated at the prevailing Public Provident Fund (PPF) interest rate, which currently stands at 7.1% per annum.

faq.q: Can I claim compensation if my contribution was delayed earlier?
faq.a: The directive from the Ministry of Finance is a recent reiteration. While it sets a clear precedent for future delays, claiming compensation for past delays might depend on the specific policies and grievance redressal mechanisms in place at your employer and the PFRDA.

faq.q: Who is responsible for ensuring timely remittances?
faq.a: The employer, specifically the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) or the HR/Accounts department, is responsible for ensuring that NPS contributions are promptly remitted to the subscriber's PRAN after deduction from salary.

faq.q: Does this directive apply to self-employed NPS subscribers?
faq.a: No, this specific directive primarily applies to salaried individuals whose employers are responsible for deducting and remitting NPS contributions. Self-employed individuals make their contributions directly.

faq.q: What if my employer refuses to pay the interest?
faq.a: If your employer refuses to pay the compensatory interest, you should first raise a formal grievance with your employer's HR or accounts department. If the issue remains unresolved, you can escalate it through the PFRDA's grievance redressal mechanism, which can be accessed via the NPS Trust website.
